issues: [MODERATE] "You will not make it past the Day when *ʿuthira ʿalā kulli nafsin mā kasabat.*" — this transliterated Arabic sits in exactly the italic quotation register the file uses elsewhere for genuine Quranic citation (e.g. *wa man yaktumhā fa-innahu āthimun qalbuh* = 2:283, correctly quoted), but it is not a Quranic phrase. It appears to be the author extending the verse's own verb ʿuthira into an eschatological sentence; the nearest real text is 13:33 (qāʾimun ʿalā kulli nafsin bimā kasabat). No ayah tag or citation is given, so it is not presented as a formal quotation, but the formatting invites a reader to take it as one.
summary: The file's scholarly content is exceptionally well grounded — every attribution (al-Tabari on ʿathr and on ẓawā ʿadl, the al-Aʿsha Maymun b. Qays verse, al-Muyassar on ʿAsr / min ghayrikum / the awliyāʾ / ẓālimīn as mutajāwizī ḥudūd Allāh, al-Muyassar on 2:283 qalb ghādir) is verbatim traceable in the correctly-paired report, and both ayahs match the canonical text byte-for-byte; the only real defect is one coined Arabic phrase set in quotation register.

issues: [CRITICAL] "The imperative fastabiqū (Form X of s-b-q)" (scholarly_note) and "Form VIII or X (*istabaqū* — there is scholarly discussion on the exact form here)" and the morphology tag "ٱسْتَبِقُوا۟ | سبق | V | imp VF:10 2MP (or VF:8)" — the verb form is wrong. فَٱسْتَبِقُوا۟ is unambiguously Form VIII (iftaʿala: س+ت+ب+ق), the same form as wa-stabaqā al-bāb in 12:25. Form X of س-ب-ق would be استسبق, which does not occur. There is no scholarly disagreement to hedge over; the hedge itself manufactures a controversy that does not exist, and the primary label (VF:10) is the incorrect one.

[CRITICAL] "The majority of scholars, including Ibn Abbas, al-Tabari, and Ibn Kathir, hold that 'him' refers to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ" — the correctly-paired report shows the opposite for al-Tabari. His block under ## 2:146 glosses yaʿrifūnahu as: يعرف هؤلاء الأحبارُ من اليهود، والعلماءُ من النصارى: أن البيتَ الحرام قبلتُهم وقبلة إبراهيم وقبلةُ الأنبياء قبلك — i.e. what they recognize is that the Sacred House is the qiblah, not the person of the Prophet, and he backs it with the Qatādah narration. (Ibn Kathir's block does support the Prophet reading, and al-Muyassar names Muhammad ﷺ explicitly, so the misattribution is specific to al-Tabari — and to Ibn ʿAbbas, who is not in the report at all.) This is an inverted attribution on the file's single most load-bearing interpretive claim.

[MINOR] Lines 21-75: the scaffolding block opens with a bare `<!--` on line 21, but line 24 contains a nested `<!-- morphology:2:146:7 ... -->`. HTML comments do not nest, so the comment terminates at line 24 and everything after it — the STEP 0 morphology table, FORM DECISIONS, ABSENCE FLAGS, ADDRESS FLAGS, SONIC FLAGS, ONE-SENTENCE DISTILLATION, and a stray `-->` — renders as visible body text. Methodology scaffolding leaking into output.
summary: Two genuine CRITICALs that survive correct pairing: istabiqū is labelled Form X (it is Form VIII, with a fabricated 'scholarly discussion' hedge), and al-Tabari is credited with the 'him = the Prophet' reading when the paired report shows him glossing it as the qiblah of the Sacred House.

Every checkable claim is corroborated by the correctly-paired report — anshaʾnā as Form IV, wa-shajaratan as an accusative maʿṭūf on al-jannāt set apart from the min-construction (al-Tabari: وشجرة منصوبة عطفا على الجنات), and the two readings of the bāʾ in tanbutu bi-l-duhn map onto al-Jalalayn's explicit zāʾidah/muʿaddiyah pair; the 'unnamed tree' point is a claim about the Quranic wording (indefinite شجرة), and the file does identify it as the olive elsewhere, matching all three Arabic sources.

The fatḥ/futiḥat/al-Fattāḥ semantics, the in-vs-idhā conditional, and the plural ṣādiqīn addressed to the believers are all sound — the last is directly confirmed by al-Jalalayn (ويقولون للمؤمنين) — and the file's three-way ikhtilāf on what al-fatḥ denotes is hedged, unnamed, and matches al-Tabari's own واختلف في معنى ذلك, with the report's dominant 'decisive judgment between us' reading listed first.

issues: [MINOR] "The verb is in Form IV (*īqān*), which carries the sense of actively achieving certainty, of arriving at it through effort... The form implies an active failure, a willed non-arrival." — the form is correctly identified (أيقن is Form IV), but the meaning assigned to it is an over-reading presented as a grammatical fact. Form IV here is ingressive ('to become certain'); the form that carries seeking/effort is Form X (استيقن, as in 27:14). The theological point the paragraph rests on is independently supported by al-Muyassar (لا يصدقون ولا يعملون), so the damage is limited to the morphological justification.
summary: Text matches canonical exactly and the substance is well grounded — al-Jalalayn confirms the dābbah addressing them directly and the 'lā yūqinūn = not believing in the Quran with its resurrection and reckoning' gloss, al-Muyassar confirms the end-of-time major-sign framing, and the file commendably declines the descriptive israʾīliyyāt Ibn Kathir reports; one over-claimed Form IV nuance is the sole defect.

issues: [MODERATE] "The reason there is no warner in every town is so that **the believers in one town carry the warning to the next**." — a divine rationale stated as flat fact, and it is not the rationale any of the four paired sources gives. All four converge on the opposite focus: al-Tabari — فيخفّ عنك كثير من أعباء ما حملناك منه ... ولكنا حملناك ثقل نذارة جميع القرى، لتستوجب بصبرك ... ما أعدّ الله لك من الكرامة عنده (the burden was concentrated on the Prophet ﷺ so that his patience would earn him honour); al-Jalalayn — ولكن بعثناك إلى أهل القرى كلها نذيرًا ليعظم أجرك (so your reward may be great); al-Muyassar — ولكنا جعلناك أيها الرسول مبعوثًا إلى جميع أهل الأرض. The file never mentions the reward/honour rationale at all. Theme Two does recover the concentration-on-one-man point, so this is an added purpose rather than a contradiction — but it is asserted, not offered.

[MODERATE] Du'ā: "O Allah — You who chose not to fill every town with a warner so that we could become Your hands in the world" — the du'ā addresses Allah by a purpose the ayah does not state and the tafsir does not support, hardening the Theme One extension above into a form of address. ("Your hands in the world" is also a loose idiom to put in a du'ā.)
summary: Arabic is byte-exact (25:51 and the quoted 25:52 both match canonical), the grammar of لَوْ as ḥarf imtināʿ li-imtināʿ, the root ب-ع-ث, the naked-warner image behind نَذِير, and the 'the fullness comes through you' point (= al-Muyassar's مبعوثًا إلى جميع أهل الأرض) are all sound — but the file names a divine reason for the restraint that no source gives and then encodes that reason in the du'ā; the old CRITICAL grade was still not warranted.

issues: [MINOR] "The classical mufassirūn — including ʿAlī, Mujāhid, and others quoted by Ibn Kathīr — said this verse is talking about people whose outward deeds appeared good but whose foundation was disbelief, or showing off, or seeking the world's praise." — loose attribution. In Ibn Kathir, ʿAlī (via Sufyān al-Thawrī ← Abū Isḥāq ← al-Ḥārith) and Mujāhid are quoted only on the *meaning of هباء* ('the rays of the sun when they pass through a small aperture'), not on the doers' motives; the motive analysis is Ibn Kathir's own ('neither sincere nor in accordance with the Laws of Allah'). The substance is genuinely classical — Mujāhid does say فجعلناه باطلا لأنهم لم يعملوه لله وإنما عملوه للشيطان, but in al-Tabari, not Ibn Kathir. Right position, wrong citation.

[MINOR] "In every other place in the Qur'an where Allah describes Himself approaching a thing, the language is one of honor and welcome — He approaches the believers, He turns toward those who repent." — a corpus-wide claim asserted as fact with no instance named, and no such set of verses really exists (50:16 is nearness, not approach; تاب عليه is a turning of forgiveness, not an approach to a thing). The rhetorical contrast it sets up is unearned.

[MINOR] "*Qadima* is the verb you use when someone of significance **arrives** ... **the Owner arrives** ... He Himself approaches the deeds." — both al-Tabari and al-Jalalayn deliberately gloss وَقَدِمْنَا as عَمَدْنا / قصدنا (We directed Our purpose toward), with al-Tabari citing Mujāhid — قَدِمنا: عَمَدنا — and a rajaz shāhid for that sense. The file builds its whole 'King walks into the hall' architecture on the spatial-arrival sense without noting that the mufassirūn gloss it non-spatially. It does concede the standard renderings up front and closes by defusing the anthropomorphism ('not a journey from far to near; it is the unveiling of a presence that was always present'), which keeps this minor.
summary: Substantively one of the better-grounded files: the sunbeam-dust image is al-Tabari's own definition almost word for word (هو الذي يرى كهيئة الغبار إذا دخل ضوء الشمس من كوّة ... ولا يرى ذلك في الظل), the 'good deeds voided for want of a condition' theme is exactly al-Jalalayn (كصدقة وصلة رحم وقرى ضيف) and al-Muyassar (الإيمان، الإخلاص، المتابعة), and the Arabic matches canonical — the only defects are one misplaced citation and two overreaching rhetorical assertions.

issues: [MINOR] Frontmatter `word_count: 6800` — every sibling file uses this field for the ayah's Quranic token count (25:51 → 7, 25:23 → 11, 30:38 → 22). 24:56 has 8 words / ~11 tokens; 6800 is the prose word count of the reflection. Metadata defect, not a content error.

[MINOR] "The second family of derived forms — what grammarians call Form IV — typically adds a *causative* meaning" — Form IV is the third derived form, not the second. The label 'Form IV', the أنزل illustration, and the causative analysis of أَقَامَ are all correct; only the ordinal descriptor is wrong, in a passage that is explicitly teaching the form system.
summary: Scholarship holds up under correct pairing and one attribution is verified verbatim — the file credits al-Ṭabarī with reading لَعَلَّ here as taʿlīl ('in order that'), and his block says exactly that (لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ يقول: كي يرحمكم ربكم); the iqāmah/Form IV analysis matches al-Tabari's بحدودها فلا تضيعوها, the r-ḥ-m/raḥim etymology and the hundred-parts-of-mercy hadith are sound, and the Arabic text is correct (rendered in imlāʾī rather than the Uthmani orthography its siblings use, which is cosmetic).

issues: [MODERATE] "Two definite nouns joined by وَ — 'and.' **Not one gift with two names. Two gifts.**" — asserted with emphasis, and it is the load-bearing premise of the whole 'map AND compass' Theme One. It is the reading al-Tabari explicitly rejects. His tarjīḥ (full text, truncated out of the paired report) is: وأولى هذين التأويلين ... أن الفرقان الذي ذكر الله أنه آتاه موسى في هذا الموضع، هو الكتاب الذي فرق به بين الحق والباطل، **وهو نعت للتوراة وصفة لها** ... فيكون 'الكتاب' نعتا للتوراة أقيم مقامها ... ثم عطف عليه بـ'الفرقان'، إذ كان من نعتها — i.e. one gift, the waw being attributive. Mujāhid in the same passage: الكتاب هو الفرقان. Al-Muyassar in the report reads it the same way: الكتاب الفارق بين الحق والباطل — وهو التوراة. The file's own ABSENCE FLAGS and Part 1 then correctly report 'Al-Ṭabarī saw it as another name for the Torah itself' — so the file contradicts itself within a page. Not CRITICAL: the attribution to al-Tabari is accurate and the ikhtilaf is surfaced; what is wrong is the certainty of the opening assertion.

[MINOR] STEP-0 comment: "تَهْتَدُونَ (tahtadūna): Form VIII from هدي ... Not Form I هَدَى (to be guided passively)." — the Form VIII identification and the reflexive-middle (muṭāwiʿ) reading are correct, but هَدَى is transitive active ('he guided'), not a passive; the passive of Form I is هُدِيَ. It also sits oddly against the file's own frontmatter translation ('that perhaps you would be guided') and against al-Tabari, who glosses it simply as لتهتدوا بها وتتبعوا الحق الذي فيها.

[MINOR] "Better than what? Better than living with the unresolved weight of having worshipped a calf." — the paired report answers the question explicitly and differently: al-Muyassar, وهذا خير لكم عند خالقكم **من الخلود الأبدي في النار**. The documented answer is not mentioned; a psychological one is substituted without flagging it as the author's reading.
summary: Both ayahs are byte-exact against canonical, the fa-qtulū anfusakum ruling is correctly attributed (Ibn Kathir's heading 'The Children of Israel kill each other in Repentance'; al-Muyassar's بأن يَقْتل بعضكم بعضًا) and correctly fenced as non-generalizable — but the file opens by emphatically ruling out the kitāb/furqān reading that al-Tabari, Mujāhid and al-Muyassar actually prefer, then concedes it five paragraphs later.

issues: [MODERATE] "before you ever wrote the check, before you ever made the transfer — there was already something in your wealth that did not belong to you. The money in your account was never one hundred percent yours. A portion of it was already **legally** and morally owed to others" and "**It was never your number to begin with.**" — the ḥaqq of 30:38 is glossed by both Arabic sources as an obligation of treatment, not a property claim: al-Jalalayn, ﴿حَقّه﴾ مِن البِرّ والصِّلَة; al-Muyassar, قريبك حقه من الصلة والصدقة وسائر أعمال البر. Whether wealth carries a standing legal ḥaqq beyond zakāh is a live fiqh dispute (70:24-25, 2:177); the file settles it as the ayah's plain meaning and builds the entire 'economics of trusteeship' theme on it. The softer version the file gives later — the relative's ḥaqq as ṣilat al-raḥim regardless of need — is exactly what the sources say and is fine.

[MINOR] passage_context: "the surah's culminating contrast between zakāh (which grows) and ribā (which Allah erases) in the very next ayah" — 30:39 says ribā فَلَا يَرْبُوا۟ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ, that it does not increase with Allah; the erasure language (يَمْحَقُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلرِّبَوٰا۟) is 2:276, a different surah. Small misstatement of the adjacent ayah.

[REPORT DEFECT — not a content error] The al-Tabari block sitting under "## 30:38" in tafsir-report-038.md is his commentary on **30:37** (أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ). This is the known heading-offset bug; the tadabbur does not misattribute anything to al-Tabari, so the fault is the report's. Reviewers of this file should not treat the missing 30:38 Tabari text as a gap in the tadabbur.
summary: Arabic is byte-exact and the lexical work is clean (s-k-n stillness for miskīn, ibn al-sabīl as 'son of the road', f-l-ḥ / fallāḥ for mufliḥūn, the distance demonstrative in أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ, and three wajh readings that between them include al-Jalalayn's ثوابه ta'wīl) — the one real problem is recasting the relative's ḥaqq as a legal ownership claim on the giver's wealth, which the paired glosses (البِرّ والصِّلَة) do not carry.

issues: [MODERATE] "From it comes ʿibādah (worship), ʿubūdiyyah (servanthood), and the Kaʿba is from a related sense of being a focal point of devotion." — false derivation presented as a lexical fact. The Kaʿba is from the root ك-ع-ب (kaʿb, cube/anklebone), not ع-ب-د. The two ʿ-b-d derivatives listed are correct; the third item does not belong to the root.

[MINOR] "The form that means sent down piece by piece, portion by portion, gradually, over time... This is not a stylistic choice. This is a load-bearing grammatical statement." — the nazzala/anzala gradualness reading of THIS ayah is directly corroborated by al-Tabari (Ibn ʿAbbās: نزل الفصل... فصلا بعد فصل وسورة بعد سورة) and flagged by Ibn Kathir, so the application is sound. But it is stated as an absolute rule of Form II, and 25:32 — cited two paragraphs later in the same file — uses Form II passive (نُزِّلَ) precisely with جملة واحدة, 'all at once.' The categorical framing overstates a distinction that is well-attested but not exceptionless.
summary: A strong, tafsir-corroborated reflection on tabāraka / nazzala / ʿabdihi, marred by one false etymology (Kaʿba assigned to ʿ-b-d) and an over-absolute statement of the Form II gradualness rule; the old CRITICAL was an artifact, but the file is not clean.

Fully corroborated by the paired report — al-Jalalayn's لا يشغله شيء عن شيء and al-Muyassar's في السهولة واليسر are exactly the scale-independence and effortlessness the file builds on, Arabic quotation is byte-correct, cross-references (36:78, 27:67) are accurate, and the one adab maxim is properly hedged as 'attributed to multiple early scholars in various forms.'

issues: [MINOR] "When you stand in salah and the imam recites qānitīna lillāh" — presented as a recitation but the word order is inverted and uncited. The Quranic phrase (2:238) is وَقُومُوا۟ لِلَّهِ قَـٰنِتِينَ (qūmū lillāhi qānitīn); no verse reads 'qānitīna lillāh.'

[MINOR] "He is not merely mubdi' (one who initiates, active participle of Form IV) — which would describe an action He performed. He is badī'" — al-Tabari in the paired report states the opposite relation: بديع is مُفْعِل transferred to فعيل (as المؤلم→أليم, المسمع→سميع), i.e. badīʿ means mubdiʿ. The faʿīl-as-permanent-attribute point is standard balāghah and the file's own hidden FORM DECISIONS table concedes 'faʿīl with the sense of fāʿil,' but the published body drops that nuance and sets the two forms against each other.
summary: Substantively solid and well matched to the report (Ibn Kathir, al-Tabari and al-Muyassar all confirm the ittakhadha refutation, the ownership proof, and khalq ʿalā ghayr mithāl sabaq for badīʿ); only a reordered uncited 2:238 fragment and one over-drawn morphological contrast.

issues: [CRITICAL] "The disbeliever is not facing divine hatred. The disbeliever is facing divine non-engagement." and "It is the absence of the orientation." — contradicts the paired tafsir. Al-Muyassar glosses the exact phrase as إنه لا يحب الكافرين لسخطه وغضبه عليهم — 'because of His displeasure and His wrath upon them,' i.e. an active negative orientation, which is precisely what the file rules out. The file builds an entire theme (Theme Two, 'The Catastrophe of Being Unloved') on this denial.

[CRITICAL] "The disbelievers in this ayah are not described as receiving recompense at all... Allah does not say 'He punishes them.'" — al-Jalalayn glosses this very clause as ﴿إنّهُ لا يُحِبّ الكافِرِينَ﴾ أيْ يُعاقِبهُمْ, 'meaning: He punishes them.' The classical reading takes lā yuḥibbu as litotes for punishment; the file's argument-from-absence asserts the opposite as established fact.

[MODERATE] "Do not think first of punishment... Pray for them, if you can. Not because they will be punished." — pastoral instruction resting on the contradicted premise above; it directs the reader away from a meaning two of the four paired commentators state explicitly.

[MINOR] "It is reaching back over the entire passage — over corruption and cycles and nations and consequences" — both al-Tabari and al-Jalalayn attach the lām of purpose specifically to يَصَّدَّعُونَ in 30:43 (the Day when they separate). The file never mentions 30:43 and assigns the attachment to 30:41-44 generally, presenting a looser grammatical anchor than the report supports.
summary: The faḍl-vs-ujra half is sound and 35:30, 4:173, 3:31, 2:195, 9:108, 3:159 all check out, but this is a genuine CRITICAL, independent of the mispairing: the file's central claim that lā yuḥibbu means divine non-engagement rather than wrath or punishment is directly contradicted by al-Jalalayn (أي يعاقبهم) and al-Muyassar (لسخطه وغضبه عليهم) in its own paired report.

issues: [CRITICAL] "Three words. **Same root.** ج-ز-ر — *wāw, zāy, rā'.*" — the Arabic root printed is misidentified: ج (U+062C, jīm) instead of و (wāw). The root of تَزِرُ / وَازِرَةٌ / وِزْرَ is و-ز-ر; ج-ز-ر is an unrelated root. The transliteration on the same line and the later 'The root w-z-r' are both correct, so this is a one-glyph error, but as rendered the reader is shown a wrong root.

[MINOR] "there is a tafsir tradition al-Baghawi preserves — narrated from Ibn Abbas" — a named-source attribution that none of the four paired commentaries corroborate. Plausible and properly hedged with 'Some classical commentators reverse it,' but it should be verified against Maʿālim al-Tanzīl before publish.

[REPORT DEFECT — not a content error] tafsir-report-018.md has the heading-offset bug: the al-Tabari block under '## 35:18' is actually the commentary on 35:15 (يا أيها الناس أنتم الفقراء إلى الله). Al-Jalalayn and al-Muyassar under that heading are correctly on 35:18.
summary: Otherwise an excellent and well-corroborated reflection (Jalalayn and Muyassar back the kin clause, the imperfect/perfect yakhshawna–aqāmū contrast, and tazakkā as reflexive purification), but it prints the wrong Arabic root letters for w-z-r, which is a publish-blocking one-character fix.

issues: [MODERATE] "Not 'their praise of Him.' Bi-ḥamdi rabbihim — 'with their Lord's praise.' Many of the classical mufassirūn read this as: with the praise He Himself has given them the ability to offer." — the paired report gives the opposite as the plain reading: al-Jalalayn glosses وسبحوا ... بحمد ربهم as أيْ قالُوا: سُبْحان اللَّه وبِحَمْدِهِ, and al-Muyassar as وسبَّحوا الله في سجودهم بحمده — i.e. their praise directed to their Lord (iḍāfah to the object of praise). The file flatly rejects that standard reading and attributes the fāʿil-reading ('praise He authored and placed on their tongues') to 'many of the classical mufassirūn' with no support in the report. The devotional point is legitimate as tadabbur; the scholarly attribution and the exclusion of the standard reading are not.

[MODERATE] "This is what the Prophet ﷺ meant when he said ḥāsibū anfusakum qabla an tuḥāsabū — 'audit yourselves before you are audited.'" — this wording is the well-known athar of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (mawqūf), not a marfūʿ statement of the Prophet ﷺ. Attributing it to the Prophet is a misattribution; the marfūʿ hadith in this area is al-kayyisu man dāna nafsahu (Tirmidhi).

[MINOR] "The unbelievers in this surah are described, in the ayah right before ours, with a haunting image. Look at ayah 12" — 32:12 is three ayahs before 32:15, not the one immediately preceding. The quotation of 32:12 itself is verbatim-accurate against the canonical text.

[MINOR] "They had a saying — preserved in narrations about Abū Jahl — that the worst thing about Muhammad's message was not the monotheism ... The worst thing was sujūd." — a specific historical attribution presented as a preserved narration; not in the paired report and not locatable as a report about Abū Jahl in the standard sources. The Quraysh's revulsion at prostration is real (cf. 25:60), but the Abū Jahl framing is unsourced.

[MINOR] "Abū Bakr could not get through Sūrah Hūd without weeping." — conflation of two separate reports (Abū Bakr as rajulun asīf who wept in prayer; and the Prophet ﷺ saying Hūd and its sisters made him grey). No such report about Abū Bakr and Sūrah Hūd specifically.
summary: Linguistically sound on innamā / kharra / sujjadan ḥāl / Form X istikbār and verbatim-accurate in all its Quranic quotations, but it overturns the standard reading of bi-ḥamdi rabbihim under a false 'many classical mufassirūn' attribution and attributes ʿUmar's ḥāsibū anfusakum to the Prophet ﷺ.

Solid throughout: the tanwīn/indefiniteness argument, the Form II yubayyin reading, the mā kādū yafʿalūn gloss and every scholarly attribution (al-Tabari on the mīthāq reproach, Ibn Kathir via Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿUbaydah al-Salmānī on 'any cow would have sufficed', and the 'they made it hard so Allah made it harder' balance) match the correctly-paired report exactly, including al-Muyassar's شددوا فشدَّد الله عليهم.

issues: [MODERATE] "The fear is named. They fear the injustice of Allah ... And then the bal falls. No. The injustice you fear is the injustice you are. ... They projected the injustice." — the file's load-bearing Theme Two (and its one-sentence distillation) treats the third question as a true description of the hypocrites, which the paired classical glosses explicitly negate: al-Muyassar reads the bal as كَلّا، إنهم لا يخافون جورًا، بل السبب أنهم هم الظالمون الفجرة, and al-Jalalayn as بَلْ أُولَئِكَ هُمْ الظّالِمُونَ بِالإعْراضِ عَنْهُ. The bal cancels the fear-hypothesis; it does not diagnose it as projection. The projection reading is a modern layer presented as the plain meaning of the ayah, not flagged as an extension.

[MINOR] "If I say 'Zayd and ʿAmr came,' the verb 'came' takes a dual form — jā'a Zaydun wa ʿAmr (singular agreement with the nearest noun) or jā'ā Zaydun wa ʿAmrun (dual)." — garbled teaching aside. In verb-initial order Arabic keeps the verb singular; jā'ā Zaydun wa ʿAmrun is not standard. The substantive point about li-yaḥkuma being singular, and the three readings offered for it, are legitimate (al-Jalalayn's ورَسُوله المُبَلِّغ عَنْهُ supports the 'one verdict, voiced by the Messenger' reading).

[MINOR] "A classical example told by the early scholars makes this concrete. A hypocrite in Madinah had a dispute with a Jewish neighbor ... But on a different occasion — when the same hypocrite expected the Prophet ﷺ to grant him a benefit — there he was, present, eager, neck-bowed." — the core narrative (a hypocrite refusing the Prophet's court) is classical, but the 'same hypocrite, different occasion, eager and neck-bowed' half is a narrative extension presented as part of the reported example.

[NOTE — report defect, not a content error] The paired tafsir-report-048-050.md has the heading-offset bug: the al-Tabari block under ## 24:48 is his commentary on 24:46, and the blocks under ## 24:49 and ## 24:50 are both his commentary on 24:51. The tadabbur file attributes nothing to al-Tabari, so nothing in the file is affected.
summary: Excellent and well-grounded on muʿriḍūn / mudhʿinīn (hapax confirmed; al-Jalalayn's مُسْرِعِينَ طائِعِينَ matches) and on the ḍamīr al-faṣl stack, but the projection thesis that carries the whole second half is asserted as the ayah's meaning where the classical glosses read the bal as negating the fear.

issues: [MINOR] "Yasīr shares its root with the word for a small amount. It is used in the Qur'an for a little — matāʿun qalīlun, a small enjoyment." — mismatched citation. The lexical claim is correct and Quranically attested (33:14 وما تلبثوا بها إلا يسيرا; 25:46 قبضا يسيرا), but matāʿun qalīlun is from ق-ل-ل and contains no form of ي-س-ر; a reader would take it as an instance of yasīr.

[MINOR] "the One who guided Yusuf back to Ya'qub through twenty years of separation" — a specific figure not in the Quran and disputed in the classical reports (18 / 22 / 40 / 80 years), presented as fact.
[MINOR] "The Companions used to weep at clouds. They used to lie on their backs and stare at stars until dawn." — undocumented illustrative embellishment stated as historical practice.

[NOTE — no over-reading found] Contrary to the risk flagged for 29:20, the file draws no evolutionary-biology or origin-of-life claim from sīrū fī al-arḍi fa-nẓurū; it reads the command as attentive observation of creation, which is exactly al-Muyassar's سيروا في الأرض، فانظروا كيف أنشأ الله الخلق. The yunshi'u al-nash'ata construction is correctly identified as a genuine mafʿūl muṭlaq, and the 'fresh creation' emphasis is directly supported by al-Muyassar's كما بدأه أول مرة خلقًا جديدًا.
[NOTE — report defect, not a content error] The paired report's al-Tabari blocks under both ## 29:19 and ## 29:20 are his commentary on 29:18. The file attributes nothing to al-Tabari.
summary: Substantively accurate and free of the modern over-reading 29:20 usually attracts; only small slips — one mismatched Quranic example for yasīr and two decorative unsourced historical details.

issues: [CRITICAL] "in classical Arabic, this is a specific, named, deliberate construction called the cognate object — al-mafʿūl al-muṭlaq." — grammatical misidentification, and it is load-bearing for the entire first section. A mafʿūl muṭlaq is a maṣdar of the same verb in the accusative (iṭʿāman would be the cognate object of yuṭʿimūna). ٱلطَّعَامَ is an ordinary mafʿūl bihi — the thing fed — as the paired report reads it (al-Tabari: كان هؤلاء الأبرار يطعمون الطعام على حبهم إياه; al-Muyassar: ويُطْعِمون الطعام مع حبهم له وحاجتهم إليه). The file's own illustration (jarā jaryan sarīʿan) is a correct mafʿūl muṭlaq and shows the mismatch. Everything built on it — 'the food is one food', 'the grammar of no charitable margin', 'the cognate-object construction without the partitive produces the meaning: they feed the whole act of feeding' — rests on a construction that is not present.

[CRITICAL] "al-Zamakhshari adds that this is one of the highest forms of Quranic iʿjāz ... because no other text in human history could compress both the cost of the giving and the motivation of the giving into one attached pronoun ... and make both readings equally valid." — attribution not credible as stated. Al-Zamakhsharī takes the pronoun in ʿalā ḥubbihi as referring to the food (على حب الطعام واشتهائه); the quoted argument, including its modern comparative framing ('no other text in human history'), is put in his mouth. The al-Razi citation ('I am paraphrasing his argument') carries the same problem in weaker form: al-Rāzī lists candidate referents, but 'the failure of the Arabic to disambiguate is itself the meaning' is the author's thesis, not a reported position.

[MODERATE] "here is what almost every classical scholar of this ayah eventually says, after presenting both readings. Both are correct. Allah meant both. The ambiguity is deliberate." — false consensus. Both classical sources in the paired report commit to one referent, the food: al-Tabari cites Mujāhid (وهم يشتهونه) and glosses على حبهم إياه، وشهوتهم له; al-Muyassar has مع حبهم له وحاجتهم إليه. The 'love of Allah' referent is a minority reading, not a scholarly consensus that both are simultaneously intended.

[MODERATE] "they almost certainly never said this sentence out loud ... So the sentence cannot be a sentence the believers actually spoke to the recipients." — stated as demonstrated where the paired report shows ikhtilāf, and one side is contradicted outright. Al-Tabari reads it as spoken: يقولون للذين يطعمونهم ذلك الطعام: لا نريد منكم ... ثوابا ولا شكورا. Al-Muyassar reads it as interior (ويقولون في أنفسهم). The interior reading is legitimate; declaring the spoken reading impossible is not.

[MODERATE] "It is somewhere in seventh-century Madinah" / "In the Madinan context — the historical setting in which Surat al-Insan was revealed" — the Makkan/Madinan status of al-Insān is a well-known point of ikhtilāf (both positions reported from Ibn ʿAbbās); the file states the Madinan setting as settled and builds the battlefield scene on it.

[MINOR] "Qamṭarīr is the adjective for a face that has gathered itself into a frown ... The classical lexicons say it is the look of a man so distressed that his whole face is collected together." — overstated. The primary gloss in the paired report is severity, not facial expression: al-Tabari, والقمطرير: هو الشديد ... أشدّ الأيام وأطوله في البلاء والشدّة. The frowning content in the phrase is carried by ʿabūs; the scowl sense of qamṭarīr is secondary and the file makes it the whole meaning.

[NOTE — this one checks out] The asīr-as-enemy-combatant reading, which is where this passage usually over-extends, is directly supported by the paired report: al-Muyassar has وأسيرًا أُسر في الحرب من المشركين وغيرهم. The application is kept personal (estranged sibling, ex-spouse), with no modern political framing. Root/quadriliteral identification for ق-م-ط-ر is correct and all three ayahs are verbatim-accurate against the canonical text.
summary: The passage's most exposed claim (the captive as enemy POW) is actually well-grounded, but the file misnames yuṭʿimūna-ṭ-ṭaʿāma a mafʿūl muṭlaq and builds a whole section on it, and it invents a Zamakhsharī position plus a 'both readings intended' consensus that the paired Tabari and Muyassar both contradict.

issues: [CRITICAL] "ٱحْتَرَقَتْ — iḥtaraqat — Form VIII of حرق. Reflexive. The garden didn't just burn. It BURNED FROM WITHIN ITSELF... The destruction is INTERNAL." (and in the hidden Step-0 block: "it burned from WITHIN itself. Not set on fire by an external source") — Form VIII اِحْتَرَقَ here is the muṭāwiʿ (resultative) of أَحْرَقَ, i.e. 'it was consumed by fire', not self-combustion. The ayah itself names the external agent: فَأَصَابَهَآ إِعْصَارٌ فِيهِ نَارٌ فَٱحْتَرَقَتْ. The paired al-Muyassar on 2:266 states it flatly: هبَّت عليه ريح شديدة، فيها نار محرقة فأحرقته — a wind carrying consuming fire burned it. The file's reading contradicts both the Quranic wording and its own tafsir, and the whole 'the destruction is internal' theological beat rests on it.

[MINOR] "إِعْصَارٌ — i'ṣār — is a Form IV maṣdar from عصر — to squeeze, to press. A whirlwind that CAUSES squeezing" — إعصار is a jāmid noun that happens to sit on the إفْعَال pattern; it is not the maṣdar of a Form IV verb أعصر in use here, and no source in the report derives 'causes squeezing' from it. The lexical link to عصر is defensible; the morphological label and the causative gloss are over-read.
summary: Exceptionally well-sourced file — every attribution I could check against the correctly-paired report is exact: al-Ṭabarī's مردودة إلى 2:245 link, his قولٌ جميل ودعاءُ الرجل لأخيه المسلم and سترٌ منه عليه لما علم من خَلَّته gloss on 2:263, al-Muyassar's زُرِعتْ في أرض طيبة, بحسب ما يقوم بقلب المنفق من الإيمان والإخلاص, عفو عما بدر مِن السائل مِن إلحافٍ في السؤال and هكذا حال غير المخلصين في نفقاتهم, Ibn Kathīr's ten-to-seven-hundred range, his īmānan wa-ḥtisāban parallel on تثبيتا, and the Bukhārī ʿUmar/Ibn ʿAbbās scene at 2:266. Saʿīd b. Jubayr and Makḥūl are quoted correctly from Ibn Kathīr at 2:261. Form IDs for أنبتت (IV), تبطلوا (IV), رئاء (III maṣdar), ابتغاء (VIII), تثبيتا (II) and تتفكرون (V) are all correct. The single real defect is the iḥtaraqat 'burned from within' claim, which contradicts the ayah and al-Muyassar. Report note: the paired report exhibits the measured duplication defect — the identical Ibn Kathīr block ('To Remind About Charity Given is Forbidden') is repeated verbatim under 2:262, 2:263 and 2:264, and most Ibn Kathīr/al-Ṭabarī blocks are truncated mid-sentence. The tadabbur did not inherit that error; it only draws Ibn Kathīr from the non-duplicated 2:261, 2:265 and 2:266 blocks.

issues: [MODERATE] "the Prophet ﷺ is described in Surah At-Tawbah (9:128) as رَحِيمٌ بِالمُؤْمِنِينَ — 'merciful toward the believers.'" — the Arabic is presented as the wording of 9:128 but is not it. Canonical text: بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ (confirmed via canonical-verse.mjs, and matching the al-Ṭabarī block in the paired report). The words have been reordered and رءوف dropped. Not fabricated and the argument it supports (رحيم is predicable of a human, رحمن is not) survives intact — hence MODERATE rather than CRITICAL — but a reordered string should not be presented as the ayah's wording.

[MINOR] "The Basran school... said the implied verb comes *before* the phrase: أَبْدَأُ بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ... The Kufan school said no — the structure is: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ابْتِدَائِي" — the two schools are attached to the right taqdīrs, but the classical dispute is verb-estimation (Basran) vs. noun-estimation (Kufan), not word order. The file recasts it as a before/after positioning question and then draws a theological contrast ('the human reaching for divine help' vs. 'the human placing himself on a divine foundation') from that recast axis. Both conclusions are defensible; the framing of the disagreement is not what the grammarians were arguing about.

[MINOR] "The word اسم — 'name' — normally begins with a hamzah: إِسْم... It's called همزة الوصل" — the word is written with hamzat qaṭʿ (إِسْم) in the same sentence that correctly identifies it as hamzat waṣl; it should be ٱسْم / اِسْم.
summary: The old CRITICAL does not survive correct pairing. Every substantive linguistic claim holds: فَعْلَان as the overflow/imtilāʾ pattern (ghaḍbān, ʿaṭshān, jawʿān) and فَعِيل as the pattern of settled attribute are standard ṣarf; the root of اسم traced to سمو on the Basran view is the majority position and matches the morphology tags; the deleted-verb argument is exactly what al-Ṭabarī says in the paired report (الباء ... مقتضية فعلا يكون لها جالبا, ولا فعل معها ظاهر). The al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr readings of الرحمن/الرحيم as breadth-vs-specificity and universal-vs-believers align with al-Muyassar in the report (ذي الرحمة العامة ... الرحيم بالمؤمنين); al-Qurṭubī's exclusivity point (الرحمن is not predicable of creation) is correctly his. Residual defects are the 9:128 misquotation and two presentational slips.

issues: [MODERATE] "this comes directly from ayah 56 of this same surah's surrounding context, where Allah says, huwa-lladhī yuṣallī ʿalaykum wa malā'ikatuhu" — the quoted verse is 33:43 (هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُصَلِّى عَلَيْكُمْ وَمَلَـٰٓئِكَتُهُۥ, confirmed via canonical-verse.mjs), not ayah 56, which is the verse under study. The frontmatter's related_ayahs correctly lists 33:43, so this is a citation slip in the body, but it names the wrong ayah as the source of a quotation and then contradicts itself two lines later ('Earlier in this very surah').

[MODERATE] "The root ص ل و carries a base meaning that the lexicographers describe as connection, attention, facing toward... The classical lexicons — Lisān al-ʿArab, Mufradāt al-Rāghib, Tāj al-ʿArūs — circle around this same idea." — three lexicons are named for a lexical base they do not give. Lisān and Tāj give الدُّعاء والاستغفار as the base of الصلاة (plus the الصَّلَوان / hip-bone derivation); al-Rāghib likewise routes it through duʿāʾ and الصَّلا. 'Turning toward / connection' is the file's own synthesis presented as documented lexicography. Note this is separable from the file's downstream claims, which ARE well sourced: Allah's ṣalāh as praise-before-the-angels/mercy and the angels' as duʿāʾ match Ibn Kathīr (Abu al-ʿĀliyah: 'Allah's Salah is His praising him before the angels, and the Salah of the angels is their supplication') and al-Ṭabarī (يبرّكون / أن الله يرحم النبي، وتدعو...) in the paired report.

[MODERATE] "There is no other action in the Quran where this happens quite like this. There is no other ayah where Allah describes Himself doing an action and then turns to you in the same sentence and says: and you do it too." — an absolute uniqueness claim with no support in any source in the report, and there are counterexamples (2:152 فَٱذْكُرُونِى أَذْكُرْكُمْ; and 33:43 in this same surah, which the file itself quotes). Stated as fact, not as rhetorical emphasis.
[MINOR] Closing du'a: "Allāhumma, You who *yuṣallūna* upon Your Prophet" — يصلّون is 3rd-person plural; addressing Allah in the vocative with it is ungrammatical. تُصلّي would be required.
summary: The old CRITICAL is an artifact. The core reading is sound and matches the paired report: muḍāriʿ يُصَلُّونَ vs. imperative صَلُّوا is correctly identified; تَسْلِيمًا as mafʿūl muṭlaq intensifying سَلِّمُوا is standard and correct; the three-actor / three-realities treatment reproduces the Bukhārī–Abū al-ʿĀliyah distinction that Ibn Kathīr carries in the report, and al-Jalalayn's اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلى سَيِّدنا مُحَمَّد وسَلِّمْ supports the practical framing. The ṣalāh-without-intensifier asymmetry is presented honestly as a composite of scholarly angles ('One angle... Another angle... A third angle'). The defects are a wrong ayah number on a real quotation, a lexical base attributed to three named lexicons that do not give it, and an unsupported Quran-wide uniqueness claim. Note frontmatter still carries validated: false.

issues: [CRITICAL] "كُلٌّ (kullun) with the tanwīn... is grammatically marked as indefinite and exhaustive at the same time... Allah did not say kulluhum lahū qānitūn — 'all of them are obedient to Him,' which would fence the group to those just mentioned... The tanwīn pries the fence open." — this is backwards, and the construction described does not exist. The tanwīn on كُلٌّ here is تنوين العِوَض, compensating for the elided muḍāf ilayh: كُلٌّ is precisely equivalent to كُلُّهُمْ and refers back to the group just named (the standard iʿrāb for both 30:26 and 2:116). The file invents a 'universal and unbounded' function for the tanwīn, contrasts it against the very form it is a substitute for, and then makes that invented grammar the load-bearing proof of its central 'there is no exception' thesis. The illustrative contrast (كُلُّ الرِّجَال vs. كُلٌّ) does not describe Arabic usage.

[MODERATE] "Notice the absence. Where is the exception?... No 'except those who turned away'... from that reality, there is no exception... He is qānit. Whether he knows it or not." — stated with flat certainty where the paired al-Ṭabarī raises exactly this as an open question and records ikhtilāf: فيقول قائل: وكيف قيل ﴿كُلٌّ لَهُ قَانِتُونَ﴾ وقد علم أن أكثر الإنس والجنّ له عاصون؟ فنقول: اختلف أهل التأويل في تأويل ذلك. The file's four 'camera angles' (Ibn ʿAbbās muqirrūn, Mujāhid muṭīʿūn, awe, silence) are all internal to the everyone-is-included frame; the recorded disagreement about the scope itself is never surfaced.

[MINOR] Element One argues مَن restricts the ayah to conscious beings — "The ayah is no longer telling you 'Allah owns the rocks'" — and the rest of the file then makes stones, stars, liver cells, blood cells, atoms and air pressure the subjects of qunūt. Internally inconsistent. (The broad reading is in fact supported by al-Muyassar in the report — من الملائكة والإنس والجن والحيوان والنبات والجماد — but that source is never cited, and it cuts against the file's own مَن/مَا argument.)
[MINOR] "Al-Rāzī sits with it in his commentary" — al-Rāzī is not among the four sources in the paired report and the claim is unverifiable from it; plausible but unsupported.

[MINOR] passage_context: "a sustained sequence of 'min āyātihi'... that runs through the middle of Surah Ar-Rūm (verses 20-27)" — the وَمِنْ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ markers run 20–25; 26 and 27 do not carry the formula.
summary: The old CRITICAL survives correct pairing, though not for the reason the mispaired review would have given. Much of the file is solid: قَانِتُونَ as ism al-fāʿil rather than verb is correct; the مَن/مَا contrast with 2:116 uses the real text of both verses (verified) and matches al-Ṭabarī's من ملك وجنّ وإنس; the takhṣīṣ-by-fronting reading of لَّهُۥ قَـٰنِتُونَ is standard balāghah; قُومُوا۟ لِلَّهِ قَـٰنِتِينَ (2:238) is quoted accurately; the four glosses render 'obedient/acknowledging' as al-Ṭabarī, al-Jalalayn (مُطِيعُونَ) and al-Muyassar all do. The disqualifying problem is the fabricated function assigned to the tanwīn on كُلّ — it is تنوين العوض, an exact stand-in for كُلُّهُمْ, and the file argues the opposite in order to ground its no-exception thesis. Compounded by presenting a question al-Ṭabarī explicitly flags as contested as though it were settled.

issues: [MODERATE] "Kullun (each/every) is the grammatical subject — so the most natural reading is that each creature knows its own salah" — the paired report leans the other way. Al-Jalalayn glosses it by inserting the subject outright: ﴿كُلّ قَدْ عَلِمَ﴾ اللَّه ﴿صَلاته وتَسْبِيحه﴾, and the Ibn Kathīr rendering in the report reads 'Of each one He knows indeed his Salah and his glorification.' Al-Muyassar supports the creature side only obliquely (كل مخلوق قد أرشده الله كيف يصلي له). The file does name the second reading and says 'both are true,' which is honest — but calling the creature-knows reading 'the most natural' understates the report, and the entire Theme Two ('the bird already knew', 'we are the only creature who has to be taught') plus the one-sentence distillation rest on the side the report's sources treat as secondary.

[MINOR] The file's own translation renders مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ as "whatever is in the heavens and the earth" and then applies the ayah to mountains, fish, dust and atoms. That application is legitimate — but it needs the taghlīb point al-Jalalayn supplies in the report (فِيهِ تَغْلِيب العاقِل), which is never mentioned; and it sits oddly beside the strict مَن = rational-beings-only argument this corpus makes elsewhere on 30:26.
[MINOR] "the most luminous parabola in the Quran" — 'parabola' for 'parable'.
summary: The old CRITICAL is an artifact. The linguistics check out: يُسَبِّحُ is correctly Form II of س-ب-ح, the physical base 'to swim / move far out through a medium' is what the lexicons give, and the imperfect-as-continuous reading is right. صَـٰٓفَّـٰتٍ as an accusative ḥāl is confirmed verbatim by al-Jalalayn in the paired report (﴿صافّات﴾ حال باسِطات أجْنِحَتهنَّ), and the wings-outspread + ranks-in-formation double sense is standard. قَدْ + māḍī as settled completion is correct. The 17:44 quotation is exact (verified), as is the 37:1 allusion. The ikhtilāf on who does the knowing is disclosed rather than hidden — the only real charge is that the file picks the lighter-supported side as 'most natural' and hangs its whole second half on it. Frontmatter still carries validated: false.

issues: [CRITICAL] "That lahā is the preposition li- ('for/to') plus a pronoun -hā. The pronoun is feminine plural — it refers back to the idols, which were grammatically treated as feminine plural (aṣnām takes this form in Arabic)." — Factually wrong grammar stated as fact. هَا is the 3rd-person feminine SINGULAR attached pronoun; the feminine plural attached pronoun is هُنَّ, which does not occur here. The actual rule is the opposite of what is claimed: broken plurals of non-rational nouns (أَصْنَام) take feminine SINGULAR agreement (jamʿ ghayr ʿāqil). The referent is right, the morphological label is false, and a reader is taught a non-existent form.

[MODERATE] "In Arabic, when ʿabada (to worship) is followed by li-, it carries the sense of devoted service directed toward a recipient... They could have said 'worshipping them' with a direct object. Instead they say lahā ʿābidīn." — This builds an entire section ('Element Two') on a choice that was not a choice. عابدين is an active participle whose maʿmūl (لها) precedes it; a participle cannot govern an object that comes before it, so the lām (lām al-taqwiya) is grammatically required, not elective. Presenting a mandatory particle as a revealing rhetorical decision — 'their grammar had already smuggled in their conclusion' — is interpretive extension presented as documented fact. Neither al-Ṭabarī, al-Jalālayn, nor al-Muyassar in the paired report reads anything into the lām; al-Jalālayn glosses only فاقتدينا بهم.

[MODERATE] "But then he adds antum — the explicit standalone pronoun 'you' — again. In Arabic this is called the ḍamīr al-faṣl or emphatic doubling" — Misapplied technical term. ḍamīr al-faṣl is the separating pronoun that stands between mubtadaʾ and khabar (e.g. وأولئك هم المفلحون). أنتم after كنتم is توكيد للضمير المتصل — and its standard grammatical account is that it is required before coordinating وآباؤكم onto the attached pronoun of كنتم. The passage's rhetorical payoff (refusing to exempt the fathers) survives, but the naming is wrong and the actual grammatical driver is missed.

[MINOR] "In Arabic, he could have answered with a simple sentence: kuntum fī ḍalālin mubīn... Six words." — كنتم في ضلال مبين is four Arabic words; the count appears to be of the English rendering while the sentence is presented as Arabic.
summary: Arabic of 21:53-54 is byte-exact against canonical text, and the thesis (their answer is a confession; Ibrahim refuses to exempt the fathers) matches al-Ṭabarī and al-Muyassar exactly, including that both they and the fathers are placed inside the verdict. mubīn is correctly identified as a Form IV active participle from ب-ي-ن, and the cross-surah citations (2:170, 5:104, 43:22, 21:51, 19 yā abati x4) all check out. But the linguistic core contains one flatly false morphological claim (hā labelled feminine plural) and two structural over-readings of routine syntax. The old CRITICAL verdict was reached for the wrong reason (wrong-surah pairing) but a genuine CRITICAL-class defect is present.

issues: [MODERATE] "Tonight, before you sleep, make this dua specifically — by name if your parents are Muslim, by mercy if not — in the exact words of the ayah if you can: Rabbi irḥamhumā kamā rabbayānī ṣaghīrā. And if one of them or both of them have passed, make it anyway." — This is a practice instruction on an ahkām-adjacent point, issued with no qualification. Classical tafsir on this very ayah (Ibn Kathīr, al-Qurṭubī) raises the limit drawn from 9:113-114 on seeking mercy/forgiveness for parents who died upon shirk, and several hold this clause of 17:24 restricted accordingly. The tadabbur explicitly contemplates non-Muslim parents ('by mercy if not'), then tells the reader to make the duʿāʾ anyway if they have died — flattening a documented and consequential ikhtilāf into a single unqualified directive. al-Muyassar's أحياءً وأمواتًا in the paired report supports the living-and-dead scope, but says nothing that extends it past the Muslim case.

[MINOR] "This is counter to instinct. The animal kingdom does not do this. A young lion does not defer to an aging lion... In biology, the old are left behind when they can no longer keep up." — Decorative analogy asserted as a biological fact; elder-care behaviour is documented in several species. The ayah's point (the command inverts the natural direction of shelter) does not need the empirical claim.

[MINOR] REPORT DEFECT, not a content error: the paired tafsir-report-023-024.md repeats one identical, truncated Ibn Kathir block under both 17:23 and 17:24 — the block covers only the qaḍā/waṣṣā discussion of 17:23 and contains nothing on the wing of humility or the duʿāʾ. al-Jalālayn is 'Not available' for both ayahs. The file's Ibn Kathir-adjacent claims therefore could not be checked against the report; they were checked against al-Ṭabarī and al-Muyassar, which are correctly paired and which the file does not contradict.
summary: 17:23-24 Arabic byte-exact; 15:88 cross-reference (wakhfiḍ janāḥaka lil-muʾminīn) verified. The linguistics are sound: iḥsān correctly a Form IV maṣdar of ح-س-ن, the elided verb (ḥadhf) correctly described, uff correctly handled as the a-fortiori device, ṣaghīrā correctly a ḥāl, and the rabb/rabbayānī bookend explicitly hedged as different roots rather than asserted as one. The min in mina al-raḥma is presented WITH its ikhtilāf (causative / partitive / descriptive) rather than resolved — good practice. The one real problem is the closing practical instruction, which turns a contemplation into an unqualified ruling on the most contested edge of this ayah. Old CRITICAL is not sustained; a genuine MODERATE stands.

issues: [MODERATE] "In Arabic rhetoric, when two opposites are paired like this, it's a recognized device called al-jamʿ bayn al-ḍiddayn — joining two opposites to indicate totality." — Misnamed device presented as an established rhetorical category. In balāghah the pairing of opposites is ṭibāq / muṭābaqa; 'الجمع بين الضدين' is a term of logic and kalām for the (impossible) conjunction of two contradictories, not a figure of speech, and 'heaven and earth' are a merism rather than ḍiddān in the technical sense. The underlying observation (the pair seals the map) is legitimate; the technical label is not.

[MODERATE] "There's a beautiful image the classical scholars used when discussing ayahs like this. Imagine a river. You are a stick on the surface... to the One who built the riverbed, the entire course is laid out." — An analogy that reads as the author's own is attributed to 'the classical scholars' with no scholar, work, or school named. The classical illustrations of qadar in this territory are the pen and the preserved tablet, not the riverbed. Original illustration is fine; attributing it to the tradition is not.

[MINOR] "Patients awaiting biopsies report higher distress than patients receiving a difficult diagnosis. Soldiers in waiting positions report higher anxiety than soldiers in active engagement." — Specific empirical findings stated as documented fact with no source.

[MINOR] The ayah reads فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ — 'the heaven', singular — but the translation and the whole of the analysis render it 'the heavens' (plural), including in a section that turns on morphological precision ('He said and, not or'). Ibn Kathir's English in the paired report renders it singular.
summary: Arabic byte-exact. The two load-bearing claims are correct and, notably, are directly corroborated by the correctly-paired report: the tāʾ marbūṭa on غائبة is glossed by al-Jalālayn as الهاء للمبالغة (the file offers intensification-or-particularization and lands on particularization — a defensible narrowing, not an error), and mubīn as a Form IV active participle from ب-ي-ن matching al-Jalālayn's بَيِّن. The mā min + indefinite construction is correctly described as istighrāq al-nafy. The qadar handling is careful and does not slide into fatalism. What pulls it down is one invented technical label and one analogy handed to 'the classical scholars'. Old CRITICAL is not sustained.

issues: [MINOR] Internal Step-0 block (HTML comment, not published prose): "scholars note that عَسَىٰٓ from Allah is a CERTAINTY disguised as a possibility. When Allah says 'perhaps,' it means 'it WILL be so.' | HIGH" — The maxim عسى من الله واجبة is stated by mufassirūn of divine PROMISES (e.g. عسى ربكم أن يرحمكم); applied to 2:216's conditional it would yield the false result that everything one dislikes is certainly good. The published body handles it correctly ('a gentle way of stating a reality'), so the slip is confined to the internal grounding table, but it is marked HIGH confidence there.
summary: This is the strongest file in the batch, and every attribution I could test against the correctly-paired report is exact, not approximate: Ibn Kathir's list of the signs given to Banū Isrāʾīl (the lit hand, the split sea, the struck rock, the shading cloud, the manna and quails); al-Muyassar's identification of the niʿma as dīn Allāh; al-Ṭabarī's zuyyina = ḥubb al-ḥayāt al-dunyā with al-mukāthara wal-mufākhara and mockery aimed at those who WALKED AWAY from that competition; Ibn ʿAbbās's ten generations between Adam and Nūḥ via Ibn Jarīr; the Ibn Masʿūd reading fa-khtalafū (correctly identified — the report says only 'ʿAbdullāh'); al-Muyassar's ẓulman wa-ḥasadan from those given the Torah; al-Muyassar's al-khawf wa-l-ruʾb and ʿalā sabīl al-istiʿjāl and qarīb mina l-muʾminīn; Muqātil b. Ḥayyān on 2:215 being voluntary charity; al-Muyassar's kurh min jihat al-ṭabʿ li-mashaqqatihi. On the ahkām-bearing 2:216 the file does the opposite of over-reaching: it names al-Ṭabarī's qitāl al-mushrikīn, preserves the ikhtilāf over who is bound (ʿAṭāʾ's Companions-specific view vs. the communal-duty position, with az-Zuhrī's marching-or-supporting formulation from Ibn Kathir), and closes with 'the ayah's psychology is universal; its legal weight the jurists worked out with care' — an explicit refusal to legislate. Arabic of 2:213, 2:214, 2:216 byte-exact. The old MODERATE is not sustained on any point I could locate.

issues: [MINOR] Frontmatter: "word_count: 4051" — the field elsewhere in the corpus holds the Arabic word count of the passage (14, 11, 155 in the other files in this batch); 4051 is the essay length. Metadata slip, no effect on content.

[MINOR] REPORT DEFECT, not a content error: tafsir-report-058-059.md repeats one identical truncated Ibn Kathir block under both 9:58 and 9:59, and the block covers 9:58 only. The file's two Ibn Kathir attributions are nonetheless both drawn from the part that IS present and are accurate; everything the file attributes to 9:59 is attributed to al-Ṭabarī and al-Muyassar, which are correctly paired.
summary: Arabic of 9:58 and 9:59 byte-exact. Every attribution verifies against the correctly-paired report: Ibn Kathir's 'not in defense of the religion, but to gain more for themselves' and 'they question your fairness, even though it is they who deserve that their integrity be questioned'; al-Ṭabarī's yalmizuka = يعيبك في أمرها ويطعن عليك فيها; al-Ṭabarī on 9:59 = رضوا ما أعطاهم الله ورسوله من عطاء وقسم لهم من قسم and سيعطينا الله من فضل خزائنه (the file even carries خزائن through into its own prose); al-Muyassar's إنا نرغب أن يوسع الله علينا فيغنينا عن الصدقة وعن صدقات الناس, rendered accurately as 'they should have desired that Allah expand provision for them and free them from dependence on charity and on people's shares'. Roots ل-م-ز، ص-د-ق، ر-ض-و، س-خ-ط، ر-غ-ب، ح-س-ب all correct; أُعْطُوا correctly identified as passive. The 3:173 cross-reference is real and the report includes it. On the sensitivity point: despite the subject being zakāt distribution, the file issues no ruling — it never touches the eight categories, entitlement, or who may receive, and it twice guards the application ('The verse does not say all unhappiness at withholding is hypocrisy. Human need is real. Injustice is real'). Old CRITICAL is an artifact.
